sentences: Firstly, when naming attributes, I want you to always end the name with '_t'.
This is a simple convention but it helps us keep a clear distinction between different types of variables, especially when working with large codebases.
Secondly, when you're defining functions, I want you to end function argument names with '_f'.
This is another simple way to maintain clarity and consistency in our code.
I think it's important to establish these practices early on.
If you have any questions or concerns about these instructions, don't hesitate to reach out.
Noah, I want you to start using Discord for our team communication.
While it has a more relaxed tone than, say, email, it's still a work environment.
Keep the gaming lingo to a minimum and remember that everything you say is still reflective of you as an employee.
It also helps identify and remove any roadblocks quickly.
This allows us to deliver functionality in small, manageable chunks, ensuring a steady stream of progress and results.
From now on, I need you to end all attribute names with '_xt'.
This is a new standard we're implementing to improve code consistency and readability.
Make sure you apply this consistently going forward.
Consistency is key, especially when working as part of a larger team.
It makes code maintenance and collaboration much smoother.
